```{r}
library(misc)
```

# Example 1: MPG Prediction (mtcars dataset)

## Load and prepare data
```{r}
data(mtcars)

set.seed(1243)
train_idx <- sample(nrow(mtcars), size = floor(0.75 * nrow(mtcars)))
train_data <- mtcars[train_idx, ]
test_data <- mtcars[-train_idx, ]
```

## Fit models
```{r}
# Fit regular linear model
start <- proc.time()[3]
lm_model <- lm(mpg ~ ., data = train_data)
print(proc.time()[3] - start)
print(summary(lm_model))
print(confint(lm_model))

# Fit calibrated model 
start <- proc.time()[3]
calib_model <- misc::calibmodel(X = as.matrix(train_data[,-1]), y = train_data$mpg)
print(proc.time()[3] - start)
print(summary(calib_model))
print(confint(calib_model))
```

## Make predictions
```{r eval=TRUE}
lm_pred <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_data, interval = "prediction")
calib_pred <- predict(calib_model, newdata = as.matrix(test_data[,-1]), interval = "prediction")
```

## Compare predictions
```{r eval=TRUE, fig.width=7.5}
results <- data.frame(
  Actual = test_data$mpg,
  LM_Pred = lm_pred[,"fit"],
  LM_Lower = lm_pred[,"lwr"],
  LM_Upper = lm_pred[,"upr"],
  Calib_Pred = calib_pred[,"fit"],
  Calib_Lower = calib_pred[,"lwr"], 
  Calib_Upper = calib_pred[,"upr"]
)

# Print results
print("Prediction Intervals Comparison:")
print(results)

# Calculate coverage and Winkler scores
lm_coverage <- mean(test_data$mpg >= results$LM_Lower & 
                   test_data$mpg <= results$LM_Upper)
calib_coverage <- mean(test_data$mpg >= results$Calib_Lower & 
                      test_data$mpg <= results$Calib_Upper)

lm_winkler <- misc::winkler_score(test_data$mpg, results$LM_Lower, results$LM_Upper)
calib_winkler <- misc::winkler_score(test_data$mpg, results$Calib_Lower, results$Calib_Upper)

print(sprintf("\nPrediction interval metrics:"))
print(sprintf("Linear Model: %.1f%% coverage, %.3f Winkler score", 
              100 * lm_coverage, mean(lm_winkler)))
print(sprintf("Calibrated Model: %.1f%% coverage, %.3f Winkler score", 
              100 * calib_coverage, mean(calib_winkler)))

# Set common y-axis limits for both plots
y_limits <- range(c(results$LM_Lower, results$LM_Upper,
                   results$Calib_Lower, results$Calib_Upper))

# Plot prediction intervals
par(mfrow=c(1,2))

# Linear Model Plot
plot(results$Actual, results$LM_Pred, 
     main="Linear Model Predictions",
     xlab="Actual MPG", ylab="Predicted MPG",
     ylim=y_limits)
# Add shaded prediction intervals
x_ordered <- order(results$Actual)
polygon(c(results$Actual[x_ordered], rev(results$Actual[x_ordered])),
        c(results$LM_Lower[x_ordered], rev(results$LM_Upper[x_ordered])),
        col=rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border=NA)
points(results$Actual, results$LM_Pred)  # Replot points over shading
abline(0, 1, col="red", lty=2)  # Add diagonal line

# Calibrated Model Plot
plot(results$Actual, results$Calib_Pred,
     main="Calibrated Model Predictions",
     xlab="Actual MPG", ylab="Predicted MPG",
     ylim=y_limits)
# Add shaded prediction intervals
polygon(c(results$Actual[x_ordered], rev(results$Actual[x_ordered])),
        c(results$Calib_Lower[x_ordered], rev(results$Calib_Upper[x_ordered])),
        col=rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border=NA)
points(results$Actual, results$Calib_Pred)  # Replot points over shading
abline(0, 1, col="red", lty=2)  # Add diagonal line
```

# Example 2: House Price Prediction (Boston Housing dataset)

## Load and prepare data
```{r}
library(MASS)
data(Boston)

set.seed(1243)
train_idx_boston <- sample(nrow(Boston), size = floor(0.8 * nrow(Boston)))
train_data_boston <- Boston[train_idx_boston, ]
test_data_boston <- Boston[-train_idx_boston, ]
```

## Fit models
```{r}
# Fit regular linear model
start <- proc.time()[3]
lm_model_boston <- lm(medv ~ ., data = train_data_boston)
print(proc.time()[3] - start)
print(summary(lm_model_boston))
print(confint(lm_model_boston))

# Fit calibrated model
start <- proc.time()[3]
calib_model_boston <- misc::calibmodel(
  X = as.matrix(train_data_boston[, -which(names(train_data_boston) == "medv")]),
  y = train_data_boston$medv
)
print(proc.time()[3] - start)
print(summary(calib_model_boston))
print(confint(calib_model_boston))
```

## Make predictions
```{r}
lm_pred_boston <- predict(lm_model_boston, newdata = test_data_boston, interval = "prediction")
calib_pred_boston <- predict(
  calib_model_boston, 
  newdata = as.matrix(test_data_boston[, -which(names(test_data_boston) == "medv")]), 
  interval = "prediction"
)
```

## Compare predictions
```{r eval=TRUE, fig.width=7.5}
results_boston <- data.frame(
  Actual = test_data_boston$medv,
  LM_Pred = lm_pred_boston[,"fit"],
  LM_Lower = lm_pred_boston[,"lwr"],
  LM_Upper = lm_pred_boston[,"upr"],
  Calib_Pred = calib_pred_boston[,"fit"],
  Calib_Lower = calib_pred_boston[,"lwr"], 
  Calib_Upper = calib_pred_boston[,"upr"]
)

# Print results
print("\nBoston Housing Prediction Intervals Comparison:")
print(results_boston)

# Calculate coverage and Winkler scores
lm_coverage_boston <- mean(test_data_boston$medv >= results_boston$LM_Lower & 
                         test_data_boston$medv <= results_boston$LM_Upper)
calib_coverage_boston <- mean(test_data_boston$medv >= results_boston$Calib_Lower & 
                            test_data_boston$medv <= results_boston$Calib_Upper)

lm_winkler_boston <- misc::winkler_score(test_data_boston$medv, 
                                        results_boston$LM_Lower, 
                                        results_boston$LM_Upper)
calib_winkler_boston <- misc::winkler_score(test_data_boston$medv, 
                                           results_boston$Calib_Lower, 
                                           results_boston$Calib_Upper)

print(sprintf("\nBoston Housing prediction interval metrics:"))
print(sprintf("Linear Model: %.1f%% coverage, %.3f Winkler score", 
              100 * lm_coverage_boston, mean(lm_winkler_boston)))
print(sprintf("Calibrated Model: %.1f%% coverage, %.3f Winkler score", 
              100 * calib_coverage_boston, mean(calib_winkler_boston)))

# Plot prediction intervals
par(mfrow=c(1,2))

# Set common y-axis limits
y_limits_boston <- range(c(results_boston$LM_Lower, results_boston$LM_Upper,
                          results_boston$Calib_Lower, results_boston$Calib_Upper))

# Linear Model Plot
plot(results_boston$Actual, results_boston$LM_Pred, 
     main="Linear Model Predictions\n(Boston Housing)",
     xlab="Actual Median Value", ylab="Predicted Median Value",
     ylim=y_limits_boston)
# Add shaded prediction intervals
x_ordered_boston <- order(results_boston$Actual)
polygon(c(results_boston$Actual[x_ordered_boston], rev(results_boston$Actual[x_ordered_boston])),
        c(results_boston$LM_Lower[x_ordered_boston], rev(results_boston$LM_Upper[x_ordered_boston])),
        col=rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border=NA)
points(results_boston$Actual, results_boston$LM_Pred)
abline(0, 1, col="red", lty=2)

# Calibrated Model Plot
plot(results_boston$Actual, results_boston$Calib_Pred,
     main="Calibrated Model Predictions\n(Boston Housing)",
     xlab="Actual Median Value", ylab="Predicted Median Value",
     ylim=y_limits_boston)
# Add shaded prediction intervals
polygon(c(results_boston$Actual[x_ordered_boston], rev(results_boston$Actual[x_ordered_boston])),
        c(results_boston$Calib_Lower[x_ordered_boston], rev(results_boston$Calib_Upper[x_ordered_boston])),
        col=rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border=NA)
points(results_boston$Actual, results_boston$Calib_Pred)
abline(0, 1, col="red", lty=2)
```
